title: Keyboard manager: shortcuts globally disabled (i.e. without assigning a specific app) are not disabled everywhere

status.label: Reproduce global shortcut suppression across editors
status.detail: The reporter describes Win+Tab escaping a global disable mapping; a commenter reproduced Win+S opening Search on 0.100.2, while another could not reproduce with the classic editor.

judgment.rationale: The original report says Win+Tab is disabled only on the Windows desktop, not in other active applications. A commenter reports that on PowerToys 0.100.2/Windows 11 25H2, a global Win+S-to-Disable mapping still opens Search in Paint. Another commenter says they could not reproduce the issue using the classic editor, indicating editor/configuration differences may matter. The current thread contains concrete maintainer-reproducible steps but does not establish whether the defect is in the new editor, configuration persistence, or shell shortcut handling.
evidence: The issue reports PowerToys 0.99.1 and says a global Win+Tab disable works on the desktop but not in other active apps.
A commenter supplies a current-ish v0.100.2/Windows 11 25H2 repro: globally disable Win+S, launch Paint, press Win+S, and Windows Search still opens.
A later commenter cannot reproduce the #47839 behavior with the classic editor; the issue references the new editor/configuration behavior.
The issue remains open with two comments and no assignees.
Keyboard Manager has engine tests for exact-match shortcut disable behavior; the reported shell/application path and editor/configuration difference still require end-to-end reproduction.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Win+S-to-Disable case in Paint on current stable and compare the modern and classic editor configurations; then confirm the original Win+Tab report.

fix_assessment.rationale: A current reproduction exists in a commenter's report, but disagreement between editor variants and the original Win+Tab scenario must be narrowed before selecting the responsible implementation layer.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate global shortcut disable behavior in active applications
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A globally disabled shell shortcut may still be handled outside Keyboard Manager's suppression path, or the new editor may not persist/apply the global mapping as expected; current discussion does not identify which layer is responsible.
plan: Reproduce the v0.100.2 Win+S-to-Disable case in Paint on current supported v0.102.3001.
Repeat with the classic and current editor paths when available, verifying the saved mapping and global scope.
Compare with the original Win+Tab desktop-versus-application report and trace the confirmed shortcut through the disable action path.
Add focused end-to-end regression coverage for the confirmed shell/application scenario.
verification: Confirm globally disabled Win+S and Win+Tab shortcuts do not trigger in the reported application contexts.
Verify the same mapping behavior across the supported editor paths and preserve ordinary shortcut handling.

confidence.rationale: A commenter supplied a concrete v0.100.2 reproduction, but editor-specific disagreement and the difference between Win+S and Win+Tab leave the current root cause uncertain.

issue_context.summary: A global shortcut disabled in Keyboard Manager reportedly still activates in applications; Win+S opens Search in Paint on one editor path while a classic-editor user could not reproduce it.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.99.1 and says Win+Tab is disabled on the desktop but works in other active applications.
A commenter reports Win+S-to-Disable still opens Search in Paint on v0.100.2 and Windows 11 25H2.
A later commenter says they cannot reproduce #47839 with the classic editor; editor/configuration path may affect the result.
The issue remains open with two comments and no assignees.
inferences: The behavior may depend on the editor/configuration path or on how Windows handles the shell shortcut; neither cause is established.
issue_context.analysis: Use the concrete Win+S/Paint reproduction and compare editor paths, then test the original Win+Tab case. Existing engine tests cover exact-match disable logic but do not settle the live shell/application scenario.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue report and both comments, including the v0.100.2 retest and classic-editor disagreement.
Read linked issue #35741 discussion: it documents a separate sequential-chord prefix conflict, and its participants distinguish that issue from #47839.
Inspected the Keyboard Manager shortcut-disable implementation and exact-match unit tests; those tests do not establish end-to-end suppression of shell shortcuts in all applications.

actions.label: Reproduce global shortcut suppression across editors

reproduce.version: Reported PowerToys 0.99.1 and 0.100.2; compare current supported v0.102.3001
prerequisites: Use the reporter's Windows environment if available, or Windows 11 with Paint.
Record whether the current or classic Keyboard Manager editor is used and verify the mapping is saved globally.
steps: Create a global shortcut mapping Win+S → Disable with app-specific scope unchecked.
Save the mapping, open Paint, and press Win+S.
Record whether Windows Search opens; repeat using the other editor path if available.
Repeat the original Win+Tab-to-Disable report on the desktop and in an active application.
reproduce.expected: The disabled shortcut should not activate in Paint or other active applications when the mapping is global.
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare the reported v0.100.2 behavior with current supported v0.102.3001.
reproduce.expected_result: Record whether suppression differs by editor path and whether Win+S/Win+Tab are intercepted in each application context.
